result.markdown:
If you're looking at the original **Oz books by L. Frank Baum**, there are several that consistently stand out among readers, critics, and Oz enthusiasts. Interestingly, some of the sequels are considered just as magical as the original.

I would put these at the top of the list.

## The best Wizard of Oz books

![(#13) BAUM, THE WONDERFUL WIZARD OF OZ, 1900, FIRST ISSUE TEXT WITH VARIANT B BINDING (1 VOL.)](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/enS1twjF5BusMI75fT3GLl71SC1CuBPP4soylLMP71ZCRYIy0VL4pnouXVyekNrd95R0mp5nliDV5d0GHc7R3JksAm05j0qFLbLQdNNBEi9VWJPyUTmXjHxnHNATC6tzx4Pr8qBEc5orWKPB5bTL1Od6I2ysmOfV5lgXrb5OsvTRs4g4ausg6Dtw7GdLDUzO?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz \(1900)**

(Essential reading)

The original and arguably the best. Dorothy's journey, the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Cowardly Lion, and the discovery of Oz. It's a wonderfully imaginative fairy tale, and quite different from the 1939 movie.

---

![ozma of oz by l frank baum, 1907 | Wizard of oz book, L frank baum, Wizard of oz](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/cPoxbpt66WDGYbRsM7-lrfg5QpCz3BaDDgu284ZuUq2u7tav1l3E4VHJjFMl0Sjq-5KogkFLdCOCC84sUsOY02dd-gnl6aY3zkgOyoC4YFCmf6lb_5T4k95-upI8T8SYC8FW8J3fL6y2m0IOMxgOGfS88MVN3iM6hAjYfLnK67irlYT1vhRJOOj3W6GM3uPj?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Ozma of Oz \(1907)**

(Best sequel contender)

Frequently considered one of Baum's finest. Dorothy encounters Princess Ozma, the Wheelers, the Nome King, and some wonderfully strange creatures. A particularly imaginative adventure.

---

![THE MARVELOUS LAND OF OZ
by Baum, L. Frank; Neill, John R |
1904 |
Reilly & Britton |
Biblio](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/sDL3NOOZ-vo8f-9C_-gE1EM9-bM0y35-oDubDa4N7XVJ9DW7NEgrlHYb1j_4Drh3r66jo69CnmIObKHvSlUYsHnai2KzmcWp5tEV3oxTUnCaDL4jlr-AWbkCWPIGN7f_ezDq97mFgnDfubP490r117lRselp_tvC11URrNl9ONVA4doNEQBhJX1DXqow7ox1?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. The Marvelous Land of Oz \(1904)**

Introduces Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Sawhorse, and the remarkable transformation involving Ozma. A little stranger and more whimsical than the first book.

---

![File:Emerald City of Oz cover.jpg - Wikimedia Commons](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/1o2SHpD-S59x4ZKCkxjNMPPafumzJpe7CuLLJ47190tefGr-8x7BQMRXAKhs9ECcbE4tMCBNs2984NFXleQcBZJTEoA3NN77VhEVen03PKWQUIsylLazDo8bzuf8Wpt0cuUvj2tZKOwz0-trS0PzZW2O1JCj4ty1iD40KZuvMH_yV7F-KaC4npIdYva--J11?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. The Emerald City of Oz \(1910)**

One of the most beloved entries for people who enjoy spending time in Oz. It explores the Emerald City and its surrounding lands in greater depth, with a major adventure involving the Nome King.

---

![Frank Baum – The Lost Princess of Oz 1917 | First Edition Identification Guide – Golden Age Children's Book Illustrations](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/8h3auWk4GJszuMT3Sw8dId0Kh8EmpTiU-Bvr-bgEAC0Mzw3NaooS26YqR1fZRftmHbRMzhueKhpPZ7KsVbiBuryBcOtarDDIu0ZigR8iNg6D6a-iBZVom2n5USPKAFFJDRefkbt1-TIXH0QG2ZwO24vg64DxrHGDhp5tGePVfBXpFJ1_X_3lc_St_kHaqqZB?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. The Lost Princess of Oz \(1917)**

A wonderful mystery-adventure in which Princess Ozma disappears. Dorothy and her friends search for her. Particularly enjoyable if you love Oz's characters and mythology.

---

![Frank Baum – Rinkitink in Oz 1916| First Edition Identification Guide – Golden Age Children's Book Illustrations](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/Z_SitQYcwDTY3XzAoyJQl4kXbc0yKMwJeH-vmKbTrMnQ1qE6EWYmcnKXCEDKF2EoJqPhRlFofYJ4pEqRswVOa4jpQsVbgkwmhHaxY0JNKNga3NlS6MXmz_3YjNo2A_zleYokEewP-n3yp7Tef0haQAId6uU0B-yt5JDtbzARvq50s5zNT63oBc0FdXnBO5-6?purpose=fullsize)

**6\. Rinkitink in Oz \(1916)**

A more unusual entry, featuring King Rinkitink and a separate fantasy kingdom. Some readers particularly love its fairy-tale atmosphere.

---

![Glinda of Oz by BAUM, Frank L.: (1920) | Caroliniana](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/0vwQJFOjdEsGD-UOCq8syCB7U4-xdDQfhbUMw1abklluF8I4h3HBDa5KWYwSbLhKB5oTYtxBnk8m742PEqHxpzGRKPsTGGszLgxlPpgUb5ofdpFshxYnlDzlWzapVEGv75yWPORhJKZd6DDDtVWYTv_OhccjGWs7rwtjH_UxJBwHkynTrSS1aVBnYBehgHZI?purpose=fullsize)

**7\. Glinda of Oz \(1920)**

Baum's final Oz novel. An interesting journey into unfamiliar parts of Oz and a fitting final adventure from the original author.

## What do critics and readers say?

A particularly interesting source is Gore Vidal's 1977 essay in *The New York Review of Books*\. After rereading the series, he suggested that the original *Wonderful Wizard of Oz* was arguably the best, but admitted that as a child he preferred *The Emerald City of Oz*, *Rinkitink in Oz*, and *The Lost Princess of Oz*\. [www.nybooks.com](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1977/10/13/on-rereading-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.nybooks.com](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1977/10/13/on-rereading-the-oz-books/?pagination=false&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Reader ratings also put *Ozma of Oz* near the top of the original series. [www.goodreads.com](https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/3242.L_Frank_Baum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[openbookrank.com](https://openbookrank.com/en/author/l-frank-baum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommended reading order

If you're interested in experiencing the Oz universe rather than just reading the famous story, I'd recommend reading Baum's first six books in publication order\:

1. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900)
2. The Marvelous Land of Oz (1904)
3. Ozma of Oz (1907)
4. Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz (1908)
5. The Road to Oz (1909)
6. The Emerald City of Oz (1910)

Baum wrote 14 original Oz novels in total, ending with *Glinda of Oz* in 1920. [ultimatefantasyranking.com](https://ultimatefantasyranking.com/universes/oz.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.chipublib.org](https://www.chipublib.org/blogs/post/chicago-classics-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

## One other book worth mentioning: Wicked

![20 Years of Wicked | Permanent Nerd Network](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hT-peH_D8cDbb7sZuOA67mmb-2mVBmR2iRzmEBk8611YKTWwzGAFJQkTIiqvB-Jq2GX-WVAHlvEMcjNXISnjaZUirvSmHgcpAiJDAv44MJm-yzu_TJ7nokg1sp2LSxbvneil_KJ17cSCev0TwFehe36I3vwGjj5zJRxI_yW16ycnSiqmelp4QtfiUHCHyHvh?purpose=fullsize)

**Wicked: The Life and Times of the Wicked Witch of the West \(1995)**

By Gregory Maguire. A much darker, adult reimagining of Oz that tells the story of the Wicked Witch of the West. Not a Baum novel, but one of the most famous Oz-related books.

**One question\:** Are you primarily interested in the original Baum books, or are you interested in the entire Oz literary universe, including the later books by Ruth Plumly Thompson and other authors?

There are some fascinating, lesser-known Oz books beyond Baum's original 14.

**7\. Glinda of Oz \(1920)**

Baum's final Oz novel. An interesting journey into unfamiliar parts of Oz and a fitting final adventure from the original author.

## What do critics and readers say?

A particularly interesting source is Gore Vidal's 1977 essay in *The New York Review of Books*\. After rereading the series, he suggested that the original *Wonderful Wizard of Oz* was arguably the best, but admitted that as a child he preferred *The Emerald City of Oz*, *Rinkitink in Oz*, and *The Lost Princess of Oz*\. [www.nybooks.com](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1977/10/13/on-rereading-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.nybooks.com](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1977/10/13/on-rereading-the-oz-books/?pagination=false&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Reader ratings also put *Ozma of Oz* near the top of the original series. [www.goodreads.com](https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/3242.L_Frank_Baum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[openbookrank.com](https://openbookrank.com/en/author/l-frank-baum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommended reading order

If you're interested in experiencing the Oz universe rather than just reading the famous story, I'd recommend reading Baum's first six books in publication order\:

1. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900)
2. The Marvelous Land of Oz (1904)
3. Ozma of Oz (1907)
4. Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz (1908)
5. The Road to Oz (1909)
6. The Emerald City of Oz (1910)

Baum wrote 14 original Oz novels in total, ending with *Glinda of Oz* in 1920. [ultimatefantasyranking.com](https://ultimatefantasyranking.com/universes/oz.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.chipublib.org](https://www.chipublib.org/blogs/post/chicago-classics-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Wicked: The Life and Times of the Wicked Witch of the West \(1995)**

By Gregory Maguire. A much darker, adult reimagining of Oz that tells the story of the Wicked Witch of the West. Not a Baum novel, but one of the most famous Oz-related books.

**One question\:** Are you primarily interested in the original Baum books, or are you interested in the entire Oz literary universe, including the later books by Ruth Plumly Thompson and other authors?

There are some fascinating, lesser-known Oz books beyond Baum's original 14.
